## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vikaṇṇajātaka* (Ja 233) is a canonical Jātaka tale belonging to the Pali *Khuddakanikāya*. According to the narrative framework preserved in its tradition, the Buddha recounted the story while residing at Jetavana with reference to a backsliding monk.

The verse text features an admonition regarding one who has been fatally pierced in a vital spot (*mammamhi*) by a barbed arrow or barb (*vikaṇṇakena*), having been struck down on account of food and music while greedily pursuing fish (*lolo ca macche anubandhamāno*) [Fausböll 1879]. The prose commentary explains *vikaṇṇakena* as referring to a barbed dart or arrow (*vikaṇṇakasallena*) that delivers an incurable wound [Fausböll 1879].
